title: Patreon stops asking AI bots not to scrape — and starts blocking them
slides: Patreon let AI bots roam free—until creators started losing income.
Now every request for their data gets an immediate block.
But bots already copied months of exclusive content before the change.
Creators can now secure their paywalled posts from AI training.
Check your Patreon settings: retroactive protection is not automatic.
thread_text:
They stole your paywalled posts.

Patreon let AI crawlers access creator-only content for months before anyone noticed. Your exclusive posts were already copied.

The switch flipped too late.

Only after creators saw income drop did Patreon block data requests. By then, bots had archived everything behind your paywall.

Protection is opt-in, not default.

You must manually enable retroactive blocking in your settings. Past posts remain exposed if you don't act.

No warning, no compensation.

Patreon never notified creators about the crawling. No tool to recover what was already scraped.

Check your privacy settings now.

Is retroactive protection toggled on? If not, your old paywalled posts are still accessible to AI.

instagram.caption:
Months of your Patreon-paywalled content have already been fed to AI models—without your permission. 🧑‍🎨

Patreon quietly allowed AI crawlers to scrape creator-only posts until creators noticed income drops. Only then did they start blocking requests. The protection you thought existed didn’t.

This isn’t a future warning—your past paywalled posts are still accessible unless you act now. 🔒

Is “retroactive protection” turned on in your Patreon privacy settings? Go check it—your old exclusive work may still be exposed.
